* mock_async works; results keep the run's duration; failures report their cause (#20)

- mock_async swaps a default-backend seam that async_compute and the simple
  API both read (it set an attribute nothing read, so tasks ran on a
  ProcessBackend); @async_compute may be used bare, as the README shows.
- ComputationResult.started_at: a worker records when the run began, so
  duration is the run's (it was ~0); TTL still counts from created_at.
- get_result chains the original error as __cause__.
- A failure the store will not record is raised after on_error, instead of
  only logged with RUNNING left behind for good.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Review fixes: mock reaches import-time tasks; queue jobs fail with their cause (#20)

- async_compute looks up the default backend per call, so mock_async also
  reaches functions decorated at import time; it warns when the swapped
  backend drops middleware given to async_compute.
- @async_compute bare detection checks for .launch, not the class, so a
  callable backend (a mock) is not wrapped as the function.
- _au_worker_entrypoint's fallback covers only the task's setup: a failure
  compute_and_record raises now reaches the queue (future, RQ job, Supabase
  status) with its cause, instead of being swallowed and its cause
  overwritten by the write error.
- The unrecordable failure is logged as well as raised; started_at is taken
  right before the call.
- Tests: import-time decoration, a callable backend, the entrypoint; faster
  TTL guard; the mock test writes nowhere outside memory.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Re-review fixes: a queue job that cannot be set up fails too (#20)

- _au_worker_entrypoint re-raises after recording a setup failure (a bad
  pickle, a store it cannot rebuild), so the queue does not mark it done.
- The dropped-middleware warning is a warnings.warn, shown once per call
  site; wrapper.backend is documented as the backend it was decorated with.
- The import-time task in the mock test uses an in-memory store.
